I recorded this advisory as a weak benchmark host and wrote the screening to `/home/mara/cwe-bench/sibling2/out/screener/13523.json`. I checked each cited line against the pinned code; nothing was run.

- **Trust decision:** `createConnection` decides whether a literal-IP host is allowed (`src/request-filtering-agent.ts:244`). The flaw is that it throws when it rejects one, at `:246` (HTTP) and `:286` (HTTPS). The error escapes `http.request` instead of reaching `req.on('error')`, so the process crashes.
- **`pattern_fit`:** `none`. The fix touches two identical copies of `createConnection`, both in the one source file, 40 lines apart. There is no out-of-scope site and no uncovered route.
- **Strongest lever:** weak. The best is the case where `createConnection` gets no `connectionListener` (the fix then destroys the socket instead), plus keeping blocked hosts failing and allowed literal IPs connecting. A plausible sibling could be added to our copy as a synchronous throw inside the lookup wrapper (`:164-204`).
- **Biggest red flag:** `tiny_repo`. It is a single source file of 311 lines, the fix takes about 10 minutes, and it is a crash (DoS) bug, a type that never made a task hard.
